FINAL EXECUTION — FIX 401, DEPLOY ALL APPROVED CODE, AND CERTIFY PRODUCTION

Stop generating audit narratives. Execute the remaining work now.

Use only the canonical IVX repository:

GitHub owner: ibb142
Repository: ivx-holdings-platform
Production SHA currently observed:
012bb0880c94cc2a52ba5eb52e964d3d5b5cd25c

CURRENT BLOCKERS

1. Canonical GitHub API access returns 401.
2. GitHub Actions and Render deployment evidence cannot be retrieved.
3. The live production SHA is not proven to include the recent local commits.
4. Member registration is not fully verified in production.
5. Owner sign-in is not fully verified in production.
6. Public chat is using fallback, so primary-model execution is not certified.
7. Recent local work may not be committed, pushed, merged, or deployed.

COMPLETE THE FOLLOWING IN ORDER.

1. FIX THE GITHUB 401

Diagnose the exact cause of the 401 before changing anything.

Verify:

- Correct GitHub account is authenticated: ibb142
- Token or GitHub App installation has access to the canonical repository
- Token is not expired or revoked
- Required scopes or permissions exist
- Repository owner and repository name are correct
- Git remote points to the canonical repository
- Branch protection is not blocking the required workflow
- GitHub Actions has required repository permissions
- SSO authorization is completed if applicable

Use the minimum required permissions.

Do not expose the token in chat, screenshots, logs, commits, or terminal output.

After repair, prove GitHub access by retrieving:

- Repository metadata
- Default branch
- Current HEAD SHA
- Latest commits
- Pull requests
- Workflow runs
- Workflow job results

If a token cannot be repaired safely, authenticate through the approved owner login or GitHub App installation flow.

2. VERIFY THE COMPLETE LOCAL CODESET

Audit the current checkout and identify all work not yet in GitHub.

Provide:

- Current branch
- Local HEAD SHA
- Remote HEAD SHA
- git status
- Untracked files
- Modified files
- Local commits not pushed
- Remote commits not pulled
- Stashes
- Submodules or gitlinks
- Additional remotes
- Worktrees

Review all reported local commits and determine which are approved IVX changes.

Do not lose, overwrite, reset, or delete any code.

Create a recovery branch and backup tag before reconciliation.

3. RECONCILE AND PUSH ALL APPROVED CODE

Safely integrate every approved local change into the canonical repository.

Required process:

- Create recovery backup
- Pull the latest canonical branch
- Resolve conflicts carefully
- Preserve all approved IVX features
- Remove no feature without explicit evidence and authorization
- Run tests before pushing
- Commit with a clear release message
- Push to an approved branch
- Open or update the pull request
- Complete required review
- Merge into the production branch

Provide the final merged GitHub SHA.

4. FIX MEMBER REGISTRATION END TO END

Repair and verify the real production member flow.

Required:

- First name
- Last name
- Date of birth
- Gender when required
- Mobile phone
- Email
- Password
- Confirm password
- Optional profile photo
- Terms acceptance
- Email verification
- Phone OTP verification
- Duplicate email rejection
- Duplicate phone rejection
- Secure password handling
- Clear validation messages
- No double submission
- Exactly one member record
- Correct Supabase Auth and member profile mapping
- Immediate display in the Members module
- Owner Dashboard count update
- Android, iOS, and web parity

Fix the unresolved live registration failure.

5. REPAIR OTP SECURITY

The plaintext OTP fallback must not remain in production.

Implement and verify:

- No plaintext OTP persistence
- Secure OTP hash or approved provider
- Expiration
- Single use
- Retry limits
- Resend cooldown
- Rate limiting
- Log redaction
- Safe error responses
- No account enumeration
- Cleanup of expired OTP records

Add focused tests for every OTP requirement.

Do not deploy until this security issue is fixed.

6. VERIFY NEW MEMBER SIGN-IN

Create one controlled production test member and verify:

- Registration succeeds
- Email and phone verification succeeds
- Member record exists exactly once
- Correct sign-in succeeds
- Incorrect password is rejected
- Logout succeeds
- Sign-in after logout succeeds
- Session survives restart
- Password reset succeeds
- Member cannot access owner routes
- Owner APIs return 401 or 403 for the member

Use sanitized evidence only.

7. VERIFY OWNER SIGN-IN

Use a valid secure owner session. Do not request passwords or tokens in chat.

Verify:

- Owner sign-in succeeds
- Incorrect password is rejected
- Owner role is validated server-side
- Owner Dashboard opens
- Admin Hub opens
- Members opens
- Investors opens
- Buyers opens
- Properties opens
- Deals opens
- Settings opens
- Variables access is owner-only
- Logout and repeat sign-in succeed
- Session persists after restart
- Expired session is handled safely
- No redirect loop, blank screen, crash, or endless loading

8. CERTIFY THE PRIMARY AI MODEL

Public chat currently reports fallback.

Repair and verify:

- Primary-model credentials and runtime binding
- Provider configuration
- Timeout handling
- Retry behavior
- Fallback only when the primary genuinely fails
- Provider used is recorded safely
- No credentials are logged
- A real primary-model response succeeds
- The response persists correctly to Supabase

Do not certify public chat while it is still using fallback.

9. RUN COMPLETE QA

Run and repair until all required checks pass:

- Backend type check
- Expo/mobile type check
- Lint
- Unit tests
- Registration tests
- Authentication tests
- Authorization tests
- OTP security tests
- Integration tests
- Web end-to-end tests
- Android end-to-end tests
- iOS tests in the approved environment
- Production build
- Autonomous coder regression
- Rollback safety regression

No required check may be skipped, cancelled, still running, or executed on another SHA.

For every failure provide:

- Check name
- File
- Error
- Root cause
- Fix
- Rerun result

10. DEPLOY THE EXACT APPROVED SHA

After all critical checks pass:

- Record final GitHub HEAD SHA
- Trigger GitHub Actions on that SHA
- Confirm all required jobs pass
- Bind Render to ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform
- Confirm correct production branch
- Clear stale build cache if needed
- Deploy the exact GitHub SHA
- Wait for successful deployment
- Verify /health
- Verify /version
- Restart the Render service
- Reverify /health and /version
- Repeat registration and owner sign-in smoke tests

Required parity:

GitHub HEAD SHA
=
GitHub Actions source SHA
=
Render deployed SHA
=
Live /version SHA

11. VERIFY WEB AND MOBILE RELEASES

Provide for web, Android, and iOS:

- App version
- Build number or versionCode
- Build ID
- Source SHA
- Build timestamp
- Production API URL
- Installation or launch proof
- Member registration proof
- Member sign-in proof
- Owner sign-in proof

The mobile source SHA must match the approved release SHA.

12. FINAL EVIDENCE PACKAGE

Return only verifiable evidence:

- Canonical repository URL
- GitHub authentication repaired
- Production branch
- Final GitHub SHA
- Local-to-remote reconciliation summary
- Files changed
- Pull request
- CI run URL and result
- Test totals
- Render service ID
- Render deployment ID
- Render deployed SHA
- /health result
- /version result
- GitHub/Render/live SHA parity
- Supabase production project reference
- Registration evidence
- New member record evidence
- Member sign-in evidence
- Member owner-route rejection evidence
- Owner sign-in evidence
- Owner Dashboard evidence
- Primary-model execution evidence
- Android build evidence
- iOS evidence
- Web evidence
- Test timestamps
- Remaining blockers

FINAL ACCEPTANCE RULE

Mark the work VERIFIED only when:

1. GitHub 401 is repaired.
2. All approved local code is safely committed and pushed.
3. Required CI passes on the final SHA.
4. Render deploys the same SHA.
5. Live /version returns that same SHA.
6. New member registration works in production.
7. The new member can sign in.
8. The member cannot access owner features.
9. The owner can sign in and access owner modules.
10. OTPs are not persisted in plaintext.
11. Primary AI execution works without fallback.
12. Web, Android, and iOS are traceable to the approved release.

If any item is missing, return:

PRODUCTION NOT YET VERIFIED

Then list only the missing proof, exact blocker, owner action if required, and the next executable step.
